newsitem.title: FRANCE: French grain use in feed rose in April - ONIC. [CORRECTED 18:48 GMT]
newsitem.headline: French grain use in feed rose in April - ONIC. [CORRECTED 18:48 GMT]

text.p: French grain consumption for commercial animal feed rose to 790,300 tonnes in April from 737,600 tonnes in March, and increased from (corrects from "but was still down from") 760,500 tonnes used in April 1996, grain office ONIC said on Friday.
The data will be officially released after the next monthly meeting of ONIC's standing committee in mid-June.
The data suggest soft wheat use in feed rose almost 33,000 tonnes to 433,300 tonnes in April, maize use by 17,500 tonnes to 249,500 and barley use by 3,000 tonnes to 75,200 tonnes.

This would bring grain use in feed between July and April to slightly above 7.5 million tonnes, compared with ONIC's target of 9.1 million tonnes for the whole 1996/97 season and with 8.3 million tonnes used in the previous 1995/96 season.
Wheat use for the first 10 months of 1996/97 would reach 4.7 million tonnes against a target of 5.5 million for the whole 96/97 season.
Barley use would reach 860,000 tonnes against a target of one million for 1996/97 and maize use 1.98 million tonnes against a target of 2.6 nillion.
One industry source predicted ONIC would fall short of its 2.6 million tonnes target for maize use in feed.
"We will certainly not reach 2.6 million tonnes, may be 2.4 or 2.5 million tonnes, most likely 2.4 million tonnes," he said.
